key_facts: On May 16, 2026, Plaintiff submitted two AT&T applications: R-107776 Retail Sales Consultant at Stockton Pacific and R-106742 Bilingual Spanish Retail Sales Consultant at Lodi. Both advanced through interviews. LTI then provided an ACTFL Telephone OPIc Spanish test expiring May 25 and stated that the rating would go to AT&T Taleo; the record still lacks the score, audio, threshold, receipt time, and decision notes. On May 28 at 10:13 a.m., Workday officially offered Plaintiff R-106742. The two-page offer identifies the position as Retail Sales Consultant reporting to Orville R. Bell at 2439 W. Kettleman Lane, $24.95/hour paid biweekly, $13,700 annual target variable compensation prorated for part-time hours, and a tentative June 15 start. It lists acceptance, hiring documents, work authorization, applicable export/rehire checks, absence of restrictive agreements, and satisfactory standardized background checks as contingencies; it does not list Spanish proficiency, at-will status, arbitration, weekly hours, or an unrestricted withdrawal right. Workday issued onboarding tasks at 10:15–10:17, and First Advantage sent a screening task at 10:19. At 12:23, Patterson texted that “the manager” no longer wanted to proceed because Plaintiff did not pass Spanish. Plaintiff accepted the offer through Workday, began onboarding, and received no pre-adverse report or rights summary. The sequence proves an offer, acceptance, and abrupt rescission. Registry use and report transmission remain information and belief.
procedural_status: LOCKED. Executed verified complaint and San Joaquin intake dated September 8, 2026; signed, not yet filed. Plaintiff confirmed Workday acceptance, onboarding, reliance, and nonreceipt. First Advantage is not a named defendant. § 1786.16 is reserved, not pleaded from the 10:19 task. § 290.46(j) is the tenth count. CCRAA is pleaded in the alternative to ICRAA. Lerma cannot run on an unattached AT&T report. FCRA may permit removal. Serve the current AT&T agent, not a store. Do not bury Serrato disclosures that day.
damages: The offer confirms $24.95/hour, biweekly pay, a $13,700 annual variable-compensation target prorated for part-time hours, and a tentative June 15, 2026 start. It does not state weekly hours. Plaintiff accepted and began onboarding. Portfolio valuation is the post-favorable-MTD settlement range: $90,000 / $135,000 / $175,000. That assumes the pleading survives demurrer on contract and estoppel. 290/FCRA remain I&B until the AT&T report is produced. Statutory remedies if use is proven: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) actual/treble with a $250 floor, fees, exemplary damages, or a civil penalty up to $25,000; ICRAA § 1786.50 actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater; FCRA remedies depend on negligent or willful violation.
risk: Strongest of the four on paper: written offer, $24.95, start date, two-hour rescission, confirmed Workday acceptance and onboarding, and a named vendor that is not a defendant. Lerma cannot run at demurrer without the AT&T report. If production shows no report before 12:23, 290/FCRA/ICRAA thin out; contract and estoppel still stand on the confirmed acceptance. FCRA invites federal-question removal; diversity removal is independently likely. Fraud remains discovery-dependent. FEHA omitted absent CRD.
